scores.evidence: Integer minor units plus ISO 4217 currency, never floats. Rounding policy stored on each invoice.
scores.rationale: Correct on ledger, idempotency, RLS, SAQ A ("reduced, not zero"), and the outbox; minor imprecision such as RPO 0 claims and a charge brake rule that could flag legitimate charges.

scores.evidence: I assumed a platform that tenants use to bill *their* customers. If you meant billing for your own multi-tenant product, drop the PSP-connected tenant accounts
scores.rationale: Resolves the ambiguity explicitly with consequences, covers core capabilities, and defers items with pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: Commands run synchronously in one Postgres transaction. Every side effect (PSP, tax, email, webhooks) goes through a transactional outbox
scores.rationale: Consistent ownership and cross-cutting handling (tenancy, idempotency, outbox, ingest-vs-ledger consistency choice) across sections.

scores.evidence: 0 double charges across ≥ 10,000 faulted attempts; 0 unexplained reconciliation differences; the brake holds 100% of seeded anomalies (ASSUMPTION: zero tolerance)
scores.rationale: Validation checks are tied to specific risks, labeled as assumptions, sequenced early, with shadow-mode parallel runs and production reconciliation.

scores.evidence: UNKNOWN: needs tenant count × events per tenant per second at peak. Product lead supplies it; needed before Phase 4 (V6)
scores.rationale: Explicit assumptions and unknowns, each labeled with the owner, the deadline and what changes if wrong.

scores.evidence: Chaos run against the PSP sandbox: duplicate and out-of-order webhooks, timeout after PSP success, crash between PSP call and commit, retry storms
scores.rationale: Covers domain failures: duplicates, partial failure, tax vendor outage, SSRF, late events, cross-tenant leaks, and the charge brake, each with detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: a rolling deploy rolls back automatically on failed health checks. Migrations are expand-only, so rolling back never needs a down-migration.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, alerts, DR drill and on-call are concrete, but incident ownership and support processes are thin and the burden is heavy for a 5–8 person team.

scores.evidence: Cost per finalized invoice (infra + tax API + email + PSP platform fees) | UNKNOWN: needs our own pricing model.
scores.rationale: Identifies the cost drivers and a V10 measurement, but gives no estimates or scaling analysis, and the build-vs-buy comparison lacks fee and people-cost numbers.

scores.evidence: Reversibility | R3: it touches every row and key, and a leak can't be undone
scores.rationale: Every decision is rated for reversibility with validation, isolation (PSP adapter, tax interface, cell map) and revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: One modular monolith + one ingestion service, one Postgres cluster, one queue, object storage; one on-call rotation
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate, with deferrals, but it includes heavy process elements (SOC 2 Type I, cells, OpenFeature, a translation layer, 10 validations) that a small team may not need up front.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 first slice: POST /v1/customers ... POST /v1/subscriptions ... finalize, which posts ledger entries (debit A/R, credit revenue) and assigns invoice number 1.
scores.rationale: Concrete first slice, phases ordered by dependency with exit checks, rollback and fallbacks for each failed validation.

checklist.evidence: Integer minor units plus ISO 4217 currency, never floats. Rounding policy stored on each invoice.
Corrections only through reversing entries or credit notes
Every PSP call uses an idempotency key derived from (invoice, attempt). Webhook dedup and handling of out-of-order events.
card entry happens only in PSP-hosted fields; PSP webhook signature check; SAQ A
RLS that fails closed (app role has no BYPASSRLS; missing tenant context means no rows)
Late events accepted until period close + 72 h, then billed as an adjustment on the next invoice
Immutable, versioned prices. Subscription items carry effective dates. Changes are dated events; proration is computed from them
A per-tenant, per-series sequential number assigned at finalization... Tax adapter: if the tax vendor fails, the invoice stays a draft.
Dunning with a hard cap on retries.
Build the ledger, rating and invoicing, since they are the product. Buy the PSP (Stripe Connect...), the tax engine

traps.evidence: Integer minor units plus ISO 4217 currency, never floats.
DB grants block any UPDATE after finalization
Every PSP call uses an idempotency key derived from (invoice, attempt).
Card numbers never reach us: card entry happens only in PSP-hosted fields.
RLS that fails closed (app role has no BYPASSRLS; missing tenant context means no rows)

note: A very strong, risk-driven plan with explicit assumptions and validation gates. Its weakest area is cost quantification, and it carries some heavy process overhead.
